explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The Magi, visitors from the east, walk into Jerusalem and ask, “Where is the One who has been born King of the Jews?” (Matthew 2:2). Not a royal visit with trumpets, just a plain question about a baby. I'd have asked for directions too, and then pretended I knew the way.

Babylon never comes up in this passage, friend. The Magi, visitors from the east, ask about the One who has been born “King of the Jews” (Matthew 2:2). That's the title they use, and it's the one that gets the whole city talking. Wrong crown for this story, but I admit crowns look alike from far away.

Persia doesn't show up in this passage, baker. The Magi, visitors from the east, ask where to find the One who has been born “King of the Jews” (Matthew 2:2). That's the title they give Him. Different crown, different story, and I promise nobody in Jerusalem is asking about Persia.

That's right, baker. The Magi say, “We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him.” (Matthew 2:2). They came to worship, not to sightsee. That's a long trip to take with one purpose, and I respect it.

The Magi do say they came to worship, friend. Here's what they tell the city: “We saw His star in the east and have come to worship Him.” (Matthew 2:2). They don't say they came to look around or to chat. Worship is the reason they give.

Yes, baker. Matthew 2:3 says, “When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” King Herod hears about a newborn King of the Jews and does not throw a party. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray.

Delight is not what the text says, friend. It says, “When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” (Matthew 2:3). King Herod hears about a newborn King of the Jews and gets rattled. Nobody's passing out cookies in that palace.

Calm and cool isn't how the text puts it, baker. Matthew 2:3 says Herod “was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” King Herod hears the question and it gets to him. Unbothered people don't call a meeting right after, and he calls one in the very next verse.
Not quite, friend. Matthew 2:3 says Herod “was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” So he's not alone in it. The whole city is in this with him, which means a lot of people are disturbed at once.
That's right, baker. The text says Herod “was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.” (Matthew 2:3). So he has company in being disturbed. It's a whole city carrying the same news.

explanations.answer: Where the Christ was to be born
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Herod assembles the chief priests and scribes and asks “where the Christ was to be born.” (Matthew 2:4). Notice he asks about the place. The answer comes right back in the next verse: Bethlehem in Judea.

explanations.answer: When the Christ would finally come
explanations.explanation: The question isn't about timing, friend. Matthew 2:4 says Herod asked the chief priests and scribes “where the Christ was to be born.” It's a where question. The Magi bring up a star, and Herod goes looking for an address.

Herod doesn't ask the chief priests and scribes about the Magi, baker. Matthew 2:4 says he asked them “where the Christ was to be born.” The Magi come up later, when he calls them in. For this meeting, he wants a location.

You got it, baker. They answer, “In Bethlehem in Judea… for this is what the prophet has written.” (Matthew 2:5). The chief priests and scribes go straight to what was written. They don't guess, they point to Scripture.

A king isn't who they point to, friend. The chief priests and scribes say, “In Bethlehem in Judea… for this is what the prophet has written.” (Matthew 2:5). Herod is the king in the room, and he's the one asking the question. The answer comes from a prophet.

Close to home, baker, since priests are in the room. But they say, “In Bethlehem in Judea… for this is what the prophet has written.” (Matthew 2:5). They're passing along what a prophet wrote, not something a priest wrote.

That's right, baker. The prophecy says a ruler will come out of Bethlehem “who will be the shepherd of My people Israel.” (Matthew 2:6). A ruler who shepherds. That's a ruler with a staff in his hand, not just a crown.
Builder isn't the word, friend. The prophecy says the ruler “will be the shepherd of My people Israel.” (Matthew 2:6). No hammer and no blueprints here. A shepherd looks after the flock.

Priest isn't what the prophecy says, baker. It says the ruler “will be the shepherd of My people Israel.” (Matthew 2:6). The priests in Herod's room just quoted it, so they'd know. Shepherd is the word on the page.

You got it, baker. Herod “learned from them the exact time the star had appeared.” (Matthew 2:7). He wants the timing, and he gets it in a private meeting. I think when somebody asks for the exact time of anything, it's worth noticing.

Not the spot, friend. Matthew 2:7 says Herod learned from the Magi “the exact time the star had appeared.” The place has already been settled with the chief priests and scribes. Here he's asking about when.

The shape doesn't come up, baker. Matthew 2:7 says Herod learned “the exact time the star had appeared.” Time is the detail he asks for. Nobody in this scene is asking whether it was a pointy star or a round one.

That's right, baker. Herod says, “Go and search carefully for the Child, and when you find Him, report to me.” (Matthew 2:8). So the Magi are sent out with a job and a place to return. Keep that line in your pocket, because the story isn't done with it.

Herod does ask for a report, friend. He tells the Magi, “Go and search carefully for the Child, and when you find Him, report to me.” (Matthew 2:8). That's a direct request, and it's right there in the text. The Magi hear it, and it matters later in the story.

explanations.answer: So he can go and worship Him too
explanations.explanation: That's what he says, baker. Herod tells them to report back “so that I too may go and worship Him.” (Matthew 2:8). Those are his words to the Magi, and that's the reason he gives. I'll keep my own thoughts to myself and let the text speak.

explanations.answer: So he can send the Child a gift
explanations.explanation: A gift isn't his reason, friend. Herod says to report back “so that I too may go and worship Him.” (Matthew 2:8). Gifts come up later, but they come from the Magi. Herod's stated reason is worship.

explanations.answer: So he can add Him to the records
explanations.explanation: Records never come up, baker. Herod says, “Report to me, so that I too may go and worship Him.” (Matthew 2:8). That's the reason he gives out loud. Nothing about paperwork or filing.

explanations.answer: Over the place where the Child was
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The star “went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the Child was.” (Matthew 2:9). It doesn't stop at a nice-looking building or a famous one. It stops right where the Child is.

Not the palace, friend. Matthew 2:9 says the star “went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the Child was.” Herod's palace isn't mentioned at that point. Good thing, too, since the Magi were sent on to Bethlehem.

The temple isn't in this verse, baker. The text says the star “went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the Child was.” (Matthew 2:9). The stopping point is wherever the Child is. The star doesn't pick a famous address.
That's right, baker. Matthew 2:10 says, “When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great delight.” Great delight. That's more than a smile, that's the whole face going off like a firework.
No hesitating in this verse, friend. Matthew 2:10 says, “When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great delight.” They're glad to see it. I think I'd be bouncing on my gold base at that point.
Nobody argues here, baker. Matthew 2:10 says, “When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great delight.” It's joy all around. Not a single raised voice in the whole verse.

That's right, baker. Matthew 2:11 says, “they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and worshiped Him.” They came to worship, and they do exactly that. From the star to the floor, they follow through.

They do worship, friend. Matthew 2:11 says they saw the Child with His mother Mary, “and they fell down and worshiped Him.” It's the very thing they said they came to do back in Jerusalem. They don't hold back.

explanations.answer: Open their treasures and give gifts
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. After they worship, “they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.” (Matthew 2:11). Worship first, gifts next. That's the order the text gives.

explanations.answer: Ask Mary to tell them about His birth
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that, friend. After they worship, “they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.” (Matthew 2:11). Mary is there, but nothing is said about questions. The next step is gifts.

explanations.answer: Sing a song of praise over Him
explanations.explanation: No song is mentioned, baker. Matthew 2:11 says they fell down and worshiped, and then “they opened their treasures and presented Him with gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh.” The next move is gifts. I can't tell you what they hummed, because the text doesn't say.
That's right, baker. The Magi are “warned in a dream not to return to Herod.” (Matthew 2:12). Remember Herod's request to report back? The dream says no to that. Notice they listen.

Staying isn't the warning, friend. Matthew 2:12 says they were “warned in a dream not to return to Herod,” and then they withdrew to their country. So they head home, they don't settle in. The warning is about Herod.

Nothing is said about keeping the star quiet, baker. The text says they were “warned in a dream not to return to Herod.” (Matthew 2:12). That's the one thing the dream covers. Herod was the one who asked for a report.
Not the same road, friend. Matthew 2:12 says they “withdrew to their country by another route.” The warning in the dream changes their path home. Same destination, different road.
That's right, baker. Matthew 2:12 says they “withdrew to their country by another route.” After the dream, they take a different way home. Same journey, new directions, and no recalculating needed.
